column2: Why can stronger gut contraction without coordination worsen symptoms instead of improving transit?
column3: Slow waves set windows for contraction, but propulsion requires spatial coordination, so stronger uncoordinated activity can worsen pain or obstruction.

column2: What distinguishes mechanical obstruction from ileus, and why does the distinction matter?
column3: Obstruction creates a transition point with proximal distension, whereas ileus is diffuse failure of propulsion; both cause vomiting, sequestration, aspiration, and perforation, but definitive treatment differs.

column2: Why is blocking the gastric proton pump effective acid suppression, and why should long-term use be reviewed?
column3: The pump is the final step of the histamine, acetylcholine, and gastrin pathways, so blocking it overcomes several upstream signals; long-term suppression can alter mineral or vitamin handling, infection risk, and drug absorption.
